title: PS12-11. Prepartum Rumen-Protected B Vitamin Complex Supplementation Improves Maternal Reserves, Colostrum Yield, and Reproductive Responses in Beef Cows.
content:
Abstract
Late gestation is characterized by increased metabolic demands that may compromise maternal reserves and influence fetal development and postpartum performance in beef cows, and B-complex vitamins act as essential cofactors in oxidative metabolism, gluconeogenesis, and one-carbon metabolism, with their availability potentially becoming limiting during periods of high physiological demand despite ruminal synthesis. This study evaluated the effects of prepartum rumen-protected B-complex vitamin supplementation on maternal metabolism, body composition, colostrum production, placental traits, calving outcomes, and postpartum performance and reproductive responses in beef cows. Fifty-six pregnant Nellore cows carrying male fetuses (initial BW = 444.1 ± 12.7 kg) were maintained under grazing conditions until day 179 of gestation and then adapted to individual pens while receiving 70% of gestational requirements; from day 193 of gestation until calving, cows were assigned to either a control group (n = 28) or a B-vitamin-supplemented group (n = 28), with supplemented cows receiving the same basal diet as controls plus 3 g/cow/day of a rumen-protected B-vitamin blend (Lactation VB®, Jefo, St. Hyacinthe, QC, Canada). Data were analyzed using mixed models (PROC GLIMMIX, SAS), including treatment as a fixed effect, day and the treatment × day interaction for repeated measures, parity as a covariate, and sire as a random effect. B-vitamin supplementation did not affect circulating glucose, NEFA, or BHB concentrations (P > 0.05), nor body weight or average daily gain during late gestation (P > 0.05); however, at 43 and 15 days prepartum, supplemented cows had greater body condition score (P ≤ 0.01), ribeye area (P < 0.01), and subcutaneous fat thickness (P = 0.01) compared with controls. At calving, supplemented cows exhibited greater body weight (458.09 ± 15.23 vs. 426.29 ± 15.33 kg; P = 0.04) and body condition score (4.65 ± 0.29 vs. 3.78 ± 0.30; P = 0.01), as well as increased colostrum yield (1.86 ± 0.20 vs. 1.41 ± 0.20 kg; P = 0.03), whereas colostrum quality was not affected (P > 0.05). Placental weight was greater in supplemented cows (P = 0.04), while calf birth weight and neonatal vigor were not affected (P > 0.05). Additionally, supplemented cows had reduced odds of endometritis (P = 0.04), greater likelihood of complete uterine involution at 30 days postpartum (P = 0.02), and a tendency for increased pregnancy probability (62.9 vs. 34.8%; P = 0.06), without effects on ovarian follicular dynamics (P > 0.05); no differences were observed in average daily gain from 20 to 100 days postpartum (P = 0.36). In summary, prepartum rumen-protected B-complex vitamin supplementation improved maternal body reserves, increased colostrum yield, and enhanced uterine health and reproductive outcomes, without major effects on postpartum productive performance.
